title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a preregistered paired experiment that tested whether inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. Using a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), a pybatfish-style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and gpt-5-mini as the generator, we executed the preregistered paired confirmatory comparison under shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate reused across arms; at most one bounded repair allowed). All 240 pairs completed without infra/model failures; every candidate passed the deterministic validator in both arms (n11 = 240; n10 = n01 = n00 = 0). The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). We (1) present the preregistered design and artifact-backed execution accounting, (2) reconcile why the preregistered shared-generation semantics produced a null confirmatory result in this setting, (3) disclose a prespecified comparison that the archived run did not execute, and (4) outline reproducible next steps required to evaluate GVR’s operational value beyond this synthetic-verifier setting.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→device-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises operational efficiency but raises safety concerns: stochastic generators can synthesize syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect commands that violate invariants (reachability, ACLs, workflow safety). Prior work therefore recommends interposing deterministic validators and generate–verify–repair (GVR) loops to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects. We preregistered a confirmatory paired experiment to ask: under a frozen, shared-generation design, does a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop reduce verifier-detected semantic-violation rates relative to a strong unconstrained baseline? Contributions: (i) a frozen preregistration and fully archived execution/analysis on a public synthetic NetOps task bank (240 paired tasks); (ii) artifact-backed confirmatory statistics showing a null effect under the study’s shared-generation semantics; and (iii) a diagnostic reconciliation that explains how preregistered design choices (notably shared_initial_candidate) influenced sensitivity and interpretation, plus reproducible next steps.
sections.related_work: LLM hallucinations and faulty code/tool outputs motivate validator-interposed architectures across domains. Generate–Verify–Repair and constrained/grammar-guided decoding have improved mechanically checkable outcomes (compilation, executable syntax) in prior studies, while NetOps prototypes and intent-translation systems increasingly embed validators and human oversight. However, controlled preregistered paired tests that precisely specify generation semantics and compute paired estimands for semantic invariants are sparse. Our work situates a preregistered GVR evaluation within this prior literature: rather than introducing new verifier technology, we measure whether a bounded GVR loop produces fewer verifier-detected semantic violations than prespecified baselines under an explicitly archived execution contract.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand: The study (study_id c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1) preregistered a paired estimand: the paired difference in verifier-detected semantic-violation rate (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The public synthetic task bank comprised 12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks = 240 tasks; each task contains initial state, intent, workflow constraints, and expected final state. Models and tools (archived): generator requested = gpt-5-mini; deterministic verifier = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Execution contract (frozen): adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; execution_mode = scientific_confirmatory; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (bounded repair budget documented in the preregistration). Statistical plan: two prespecified primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B) with Bonferroni correction (family alpha = 0.05 → per-comparison alpha = 0.025). Primary test: exact McNemar two-sided; paired-bootstrap 95% CIs (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Preregistration also specified conservative sensitivity analyses and contamination checks; all analysis code and artifacts are archived.
sections.results: Artifact-backed execution accounting: planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; complete_pair_count = 240; model_calls_used = 240 (shared-initial-candidate design produced one model call per task reused across arms; stage_counts recorded as {"shared_initial_generation": 240}). Primary contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 240 (both arms accepted), n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired estimate and inference (analysis/results.json): rate_GVR − rate_baseline = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Repair application: repair_applied = false for all episodes because the shared initial candidate satisfied the verifier predicates in every task (representative scoring artifacts under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/). Missingness and exclusions: complete_pairs = 240; failed episodes = 0; no exclusions applied. Prespecified comparison status: the preregistration listed two primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B); the archived run executed only C vs A (GVR vs unconstrained baseline) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The prespecified C vs B (GVR vs schema-constrained baseline) was not executed and the execution artifacts contain no recorded rationale for that omission; we report this omission explicitly as a prespecified but unexecuted analysis.
sections.discussion: Interpretation and design reconciliation: the null confirmatory result is artifact-grounded and expected under the archived semantics: reusing a single initial candidate per task meant the generator’s shared output already satisfied verifier predicates for this synthetic task distribution and prompting, so the bounded repair stage never triggered. Two non-exclusive, artifact-backed explanations account for this outcome: (1) task/verifier match — the synthetic tasks plus the verifier predicates created a distribution the generator could satisfy reliably under the supplied prompting; and (2) sensitivity reduction from shared-generation semantics — shared_initial_candidate removes per-arm stochastic variation that an independent-sampling design would expose and that GVR could potentially exploit. Power and inferential consequences: the preregistration’s power calculation (targeting ~10 percentage-point paired reduction with N=240) assumed the ability to observe discordant pairs under independent per-condition generation. Because execution used shared_initial_candidate, those power assumptions do not apply to the archived execution; consequently the archived null result is a valid empirical observation for the executed design but should not be interpreted as evidence that GVR is ineffective under independent-generation or adversarial distributions. Multiplicity: Bonferroni correction for two prespecified comparisons was preregistered; because only one prespecified comparison was executed, the posted p-value corresponds to the single executed comparison and no Bonferroni adjustment was applied. Procedural note: the archived artifacts do not record a rationale for the omitted prespecified comparison (C vs B); we therefore treat its omission as an unresolved procedural limitation and report it transparently. Recommended reproducible follow-ups (consistent with preregistered planned outputs): (i) rerun with independent per-condition generation (remove shared_initial_candidate) to restore discordance potential; (ii) inject adversarial/golden tasks designed to violate verifier predicates and measure repair utilization; (iii) evaluate multiple generator families and prompt variants; and (iv) integrate stronger semantic/formal verifiers (SMT/constraint hybrids) to widen oracle coverage. These steps are required before generalizing about GVR’s operational benefits beyond the tested synthetic-verifier setting.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment testing a bounded GVR intervention on a synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task bank. Under the preregistered shared-initial-candidate semantics, every initial candidate passed the deterministic validator in both arms (n = 240 pairs), producing a null confirmatory result: paired estimate = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.00; 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. The artifacts are authoritative for these numbers. The result demonstrates that (a) when generator+prompting already satisfy verifier predicates on a task distribution, a bounded GVR loop may be redundant for those predicates, and (b) to evaluate GVR’s operational value one must run independent-generation, adversarial, and multi-model experiments and adopt stronger semantic or formal verifiers to measure residual risks outside the current oracle. We release the archived artifacts so the community can reproduce the accounting and extend the evaluation under alternative generation semantics and adversarial conditions.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but also reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
